groups.title: Pinia State Management
groups.question: Your Nuxt app's cart store refetches on every page load even though the server already loaded it. Explain how Pinia stores are defined and hydrated in SSR.

followUps.Store Definition: Options vs Setup Synta: What is the difference between an options store and a setup store?
followUps.Store Hydration in SSR: How does store state get from the server to the client?

evidence.text: An options store uses state, getters and actions objects.
A setup store uses a function with refs and computed.
Setup stores are more flexible and can use composables inside.

notEnough: Only saying there are two syntaxes.

evidence.text: Store state filled on the server is serialised into the page.
The client restores it during hydration.
The data is not fetched again on page load.

groups.title: Authentication Patterns
groups.question: You are adding login to your Nuxt app and protecting the dashboard. Explain how sessions and route middleware work.

followUps.Route Protection with Middleware: How does route middleware protect pages, and is that enough?

evidence.text: Sessions are stored in an encrypted, sealed cookie.
useUserSession reads the session on both server and client.
No session database is needed for the basic setup.
Route middleware runs before navigation, on server and client.
It redirects users who are not logged in.
Server API routes must still check the session themselves.

groups.title: TypeScript with Pinia
groups.question: Your Pinia store has complex state and you want type errors when components misuse it. Explain how types and getters work in Pinia.

followUps.Typing Store State and Actions: How does Pinia infer types, and when should you type state explicitly?

evidence.text: Pinia infers types from the state and actions.
Complex or nullable state is typed explicitly with interfaces.
Components then get type errors for wrong usage.
Getters work like computed properties.
They are cached and recompute only when their dependencies change.
They hold derived values, like a cart total.

groups.title: Security Considerations
groups.question: A security review asks how your Nuxt app stops cross-site request forgery and how passwords are stored. Explain your protections.

followUps.CSRF Protection in Nuxt: How do you protect cookie-based sessions from CSRF?
followUps.Password Hashing with bcrypt/argon2: Why use bcrypt or argon2 instead of MD5 or SHA1?

evidence.text: Cookies are sent automatically, so other sites can trigger requests with them.
SameSite cookies stop sending them on most cross-site requests.
For sensitive actions, checking the origin or using tokens adds protection.
bcrypt and argon2 are deliberately slow and salted.
Fast hashes like MD5 or SHA1 can be cracked quickly after a leak.
Their cost setting can be raised over time.
